chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Mas‘adah ibn Ziyad, from Abu ‘Abdillah; and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibrahim, from Abu Yahya al-Mada’ini, from Abu Harun al-‘Abdi, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said:

I was present when Abu Bakr died and appointed ‘Umar. A Jew from the leading men of the Jews of Yathrib came forward, and the Jews of al-Madinah claimed that he was the most knowledgeable of the people of his time, until he was brought to ‘Umar. He said to him: “O ‘Umar, I have come to you desiring Islam. If you inform me about what I ask you concerning, then you are the most knowledgeable of the companions of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the Book, the sunnah, and all that I wish to ask about.”

He said: ‘Umar said to him: “I am not in that rank, but I shall direct you to the one who is the most knowledgeable of our ummah regarding the Book, the sunnah, and all that you may ask about, and he is that one.” He then pointed to ‘Ali عليه السلام. The Jew said to him: “O ‘Umar, if this is as you say, then what right have you to the people’s bay‘ah, when that one is the most knowledgeable among you?” So ‘Umar rebuked him.

Then the Jew went to ‘Ali عليه السلام and said to him: “Are you as ‘Umar described?” He said: “And what did ‘Umar say?” So he informed him. He said: “If you are as he said, I will ask you about matters which I wish to know whether anyone among you knows them, so that I may know that in your claim you are the best of communities and the most truthful of them; and with that, I will enter into your religion, Islam.”

Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام said: “Yes, I am as ‘Umar described to you. Ask whatever occurs to you, and I will inform you of it, if Allah wills.” He said: “Inform me about three, and three, and one.” ‘Ali عليه السلام said to him: “O Jew, why did you not say: inform me about seven?” The Jew said to him: “If you inform me of the three, I shall ask you about the rest; otherwise, I shall refrain. If you answer me regarding these seven, then you are the most knowledgeable of the people of the earth, the most excellent of them, and the worthiest of people over the people.”

He said to him: “Ask whatever occurs to you, O Jew.” He said: “Inform me about the first stone placed upon the face of the earth, the first tree planted upon the face of the earth, and the first spring that gushed forth upon the face of the earth.” Then Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام informed him.

Then the Jew said to him: “Inform me about this ummah: how many Imams of guidance does it have? And inform me about your Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: where is his منزل in Paradise? And inform me who will be with him in Paradise.” Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام said to him: “Indeed, this ummah has twelve Imams of guidance from the progeny of its Prophet, and they are from me. As for the abode of our Prophet in Paradise, it is in the best and noblest part of it, in Jannat ‘Adn. And as for those who are with him in his abode therein, they are these twelve from his progeny, and their mother, and their grandmother, and the mother of their mother, and their offspring; no one shares it with them.”

key_terms.أَعْلَمُ: most knowledgeable, denoting superiority in sacred knowledge
key_terms.إِمَامٍ هُدًى: an Imam of guidance, a divinely guided leader for the ummah
key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the sunnah, the normative prophetic tradition
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the eternal abode of reward
key_terms.الْكِتَابِ: the revealed Book, meaning divine scripture as a source of guidance
key_terms.جَنَّةِ عَدْنٍ: the Garden of Eden, described here as the highest and noblest part of Paradise
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّةِ: progeny or offspring, referring to the descendants of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi say about Imam ‘Ali عليه السلام and the twelve Imams of guidance?
ai.summary: This narration recounts a Jewish scholar testing the knowledge of ‘Umar, who directs him to Imam ‘Ali عليه السلام as the most knowledgeable member of the ummah in the Book and the sunnah. The hadith highlights the special knowledge and authority of Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام and includes his statement that this ummah has twelve Imams of guidance from the progeny of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, along with a description of the Prophet’s abode in Paradise.
